how: We read the website of every Atlanta wedding photographer listed on Lazo (122 listings, 91 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: a national photo-and-DJ chain's Atlanta page, a Nashville photographer with no Atlanta presence, portrait, pet and tintype studios, photo booth companies, and a DJ and decor company listed as a photographer. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: How do you handle a July ceremony in direct sun and humidity, and what time do you want portraits so nobody is wilting?
Can I see a full gallery from one wedding at a venue like mine, not a highlight reel?
What is the delivery timeline, and is a second shooter included or an add-on?

picks.name: Danielle Brown Photography
picks.blurb: Dani Brown's Marietta studio has photographed Atlanta weddings since 2009, first as It's Your Day Photography and, after a late 2016 rebrand, as Danielle Brown Photography & Film. The coverage list runs from getting ready through the start of the reception, with digital JPEG delivery.

picks.name: Meli & Chris Wedding Photography
picks.blurb: A husband-and-wife team based in Atlanta who have photographed celebrations at more than 125 venues across the Southeast, plus destination weddings abroad. Meli and Chris describe a timeless editing style and offer timeline guidance before the day.

picks.name: Atlanta Artistic Wedding photographers
picks.blurb: David Diener leads a team of Atlanta wedding photographers and videographers who describe themselves as combining creativity, artistry and affordability. The site makes a point of the whole team showing up for each other at every wedding.

picks.name: Double N Media
picks.blurb: Lindsay has photographed Atlanta weddings for more than ten years and says the job is about relationships as much as the camera: guiding you, helping you relax and keeping you in the moment. Now booking Atlanta and North Georgia, with an Investment page on the site.

picks.name: Elicia Bryan Photography
picks.blurb: Self-described anti-cliche, Elicia Bryan brings a laid-back, artful approach, photographing things as naturally as they happen for weddings, elopements and couples. Based in Atlanta and traveling worldwide, she says the compliment she hears most is how easy she makes being photographed.

picks.name: Denis Reggie Photographers
picks.blurb: Denis Reggie is a wedding photojournalist based in Atlanta who took up the camera as a Louisiana teenager after a football injury ended his playing days, and the site identifies him as a Canon Legend. Authenticity is the stated focus of the work.

picks.name: C Brown Photo
picks.blurb: Cindy shoots documentary wedding photography she calls delightfully fun: real connections, tiny details and relaxed, fast portraits instead of stiff poses. Coverage is customized, she says she loves elopements and smaller weddings, and the site cites a top WPJA documentary ranking for the Americas in 2025.

picks.name: Brianna Marie Photography
picks.blurb: Bree is a West Georgia wedding and lifestyle photographer with an editorial but honest perspective, aimed at anyone who has ever felt they are not photogenic. Custom collections on request, LGBT friendly, and willing to travel anywhere in the United States.

picks.name: Love & Story Photography
picks.blurb: Vania and Martine are two best friends who run Love & Story out of Roswell, with packages sized for city hall, micro weddings and full luxury celebrations. Their style is bold color, epic and romantic, and the site talks openly about what Atlanta wedding photography costs.

picks.name: Michelle Scott Photography
picks.blurb: Originally a painter, Michelle Scott is an Atlanta and New York editorial wedding photographer with more than 12 years of experience, shooting film and digital with a fine art, documentary approach. Preserving true color and nostalgia is her stated fascination.

picks.name: The Decisive Moment Wedding Photojournalism
picks.blurb: A Chamblee studio built around a team: a studio director handles your custom package, shot lists and timelines with you and your coordinator, so the photographers concentrate on shooting. The Decisive Moment works in a photojournalistic style and dates its start to 2005.

picks.name: Just Peachy Wedding Photography
picks.blurb: Anthony Stalcup spent most of his 20-plus years as a photojournalist and editorial photographer before Just Peachy, which he describes as a one-stop Atlanta-area wedding photo provider with video packages available. Based in Woodstock.
